headline: Customers are signing year-long deals for AI chip testing capacity, and testing firm Sigurd has begun raising prices.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a sector roundup; the supplier confirmed its own price rises.
importance_line: What changed: testing is a tighter bottleneck and a rising cost for AI chips, which matters most to chip buyers who now have to commit a year ahead; Sigurd confirmed its price rises, but the figures come from several outlets and the test-time estimates are Nomura's, not measured results.
summary: TrendForce reports, citing STAR Market Daily, that customers of chip testing firm Sigurd Microelectronics are signing deals of more than a year to secure capacity, and that Sigurd has begun raising its own prices. Testing is getting harder and costlier as AI chips take longer to check: according to Nomura Securities, as cited by Seoul Economic Daily, Nvidia's Blackwell chip needs an estimated four times the final test time of Hopper, and Rubin could need seven times as long.
notes: Read in full. Mixed chain: TrendForce cites STAR Market Daily, Seoul Economic Daily (citing Nomura), TechNews and ETNews.
